summary: Defines the Robust XML Encoding Rules (RXER), a set of ASN.1 encoding rules that produce an XML representation of values of any ASN.1 data type. It also defines a canonical form. It is an experimental protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RXER defines how to represent ASN.1 data as XML. Its canonical form, CRXER, removes encoding choices so a given ASN.1 value can be serialized consistently.

questions: how to encode asn.1 as xml
what is the difference between rxer and crxer
why use xml for asn.1 encoding
when should rxer not be used
subtitle: Rules for representing ASN.1 values as XML, with a canonical form for consistent serialization.

tldr.problem: ASN.1 defines data types, but applications that need XML interchange require rules for representing those values as XML and preserving consistent meaning.
tldr.mechanism: RXER maps ASN.1 values to XML elements, attributes and text. CRXER restricts serialization choices so the same abstract value has one canonical XML encoding.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4910 is Experimental. It warns that RXER cannot preserve recoverable original encodings for certain ASN.1 string types and that XML cannot represent the null character.

facts.label: Canonical encoding
facts.value: One serialization for each ASN.1 value

today: RFC 4910 is Experimental and defines XML encoding rules for ASN.1 values. The RFC metadata lists no document that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: ASN.1 Values in XML
sections.content:
Robust XML Encoding Rules (RXER) encode values of ASN.1 types as XML. Simple types such as integers and Boolean values become character data or attribute values. Combining types such as SEQUENCE and SET use XML elements and attributes corresponding to their named components.

The RFC defines RXER as an alternative encoding for an ASN.1 value, not as a conversion of an existing BER byte sequence. It also defines CRXER, a restricted form that produces a canonical encoding.
sections.plainLanguage: ASN.1 describes the data and its types; RXER specifies how that data appears in XML. The XML represents the ASN.1 value, not an existing BER encoding.

sections.title: Encoding Types and Components
sections.content:
RXER maps an ASN.1 module to an XML namespace. Names of components in ASN.1 definitions generally become the names of XML elements or attributes. Character-string values can appear as text; other types have rules for their own values and structures.

The RFC defines additional ASN.1 types, including Markup for holding XML element content and attributes, and QName for qualified names. Markup values must be self-contained so their namespace meanings do not depend on an enclosing element.
sections.plainLanguage: RXER uses the ASN.1 definition to determine XML names and structure. A Markup value must carry the namespace information needed to interpret its own content.

sections.title: Canonical RXER
sections.content:
Ordinary RXER allows some serialization choices, so more than one XML document can represent the same ASN.1 value. Canonical RXER (CRXER) restricts those choices, including namespace prefixes, attribute ordering and whitespace, to produce one canonical XML representation.

CRXER uses a defined serialization, including UTF-8 and a specified XML declaration. A canonical form is useful when systems need matching encoded values, but the RFC also requires syntax-based XML canonicalization to account for RXER encodings before applying it.
sections.plainLanguage: Two valid RXER encodings of the same value can differ in details. CRXER fixes those details so the same value produces one consistent XML form.

sections.title: Limits for Recovering Encodings
sections.content:
RXER may not preserve enough information to reconstruct the exact original DER or CER encoding for values using TeletexString, VideotexString, GraphicString or GeneralString. The RFC says not to use RXER to re-encode such values when the original DER or CER encoding must be recoverable, as for verifying some digital signatures.

XML cannot represent the null character, so RXER encoding drops null characters in ASN.1 strings. Implementations must compare security-sensitive fields using their underlying abstract values, not differences in the XML encoding.
sections.plainLanguage: RXER cannot preserve every original byte encoding, and XML cannot carry a null character. Do not use it where those details must be recovered, such as verifying certain signatures.
